text: Chairman, we are encouraged that HDB has cleared the BTO backlog from the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: About 13,000 flats will reach their five-year MOP in 2026, nearly double that of last year.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: With supply improving and price pressure easing, this is the right moment to finetune the eligibility policy so more Singaporeans can access affordable housing while keeping the market stable and fiscally responsible.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: First, I urge the HDB to review the BTO eligibility age for singles, with consideration to lower to 30 years old.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: So, 30 years old, we let the singles buy a BTO flat.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Many singles today seek stability earlier, shoulder family responsibilities and want to build their own future.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: A home gives not just a shelter but dignity, security and a stake in the society.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Second, we could update the BTO income ceiling for first-timer families.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: The $14,000 cap has not changed since 2019 even though nominal wages have risen by more than 25%.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: More young couples are now squeezed above the BTO income ceiling, yet are unable to afford private housing or executive condominiums.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Raising the ceiling to $16,000 keeps public housing accessible to the broad middle group of Singaporeans, in line with economic realities.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Third, I hope MND can waive the 15-month wait-out period to buy a HDB 4-room or smaller resale flat after a private property owner sells the private property due to difficult life transitions such as divorce or financial strain.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Chairman, when supply improves, policy needs to keep pace.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Housing is not just about markets, it is about people.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Members for their questions and suggestions.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Over the past 60 years, we have worked hard to build Singapore together.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We provided Singaporeans with affordable and accessible public housing and achieved one of the highest homeownership rates in the world.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We developed a strong built environment sector, which can plan, construct and maintain large-scale projects efficiently in our dense urban setting.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We have carefully balanced the needs of current and future generations through long-term planning, integrating different uses and maximising the overall value of our limited land.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We need to build on these strong foundations and go further.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: At this year's COS, I would like to present three key priorities that MND will focus on for the next few years.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: First, we will continue to uphold our housing commitments and sustain a robust supply.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We will build more and build faster to meet the evolving housing needs of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Senior Minister of State Sun and Senior Parliamentary Secretary Harun will elaborate on our efforts to enhance the liveability of HDB estates.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Minister Indranee and Minister of State Tan will talk about our plans to enhance the liveability of private residential estates and our City in Nature.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Second, we will continue transforming our built environment sector to achieve greater productivity, sustainability and resilience and create more good jobs for our people.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Third, Minister of State Tan will round up by sharing more about our longer-term plans for Singapore's development, balancing the different land use requirements and navigating trade-offs within the limited space we have.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We provided a strong supply of HDB flats and set aside more units for first-timer families.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This is good news, but the overall application rate for 3-room and bigger BTO flats was 2.6 times, if we include second-timer families.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The application rates for singles and seniors for 2-room Flexi flats were also higher.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These numbers reflect the continued strong demand for public housing and why we need to sustain a robust supply in the years ahead.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We now have some capacity to meet additional housing needs of different groups of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Many Members, including Mr Henry Kwek, Mr Foo Cexiang and Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin, have asked about this.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We will support our seniors by offering different right-sizing and monetisation options and making our neighbourhoods more elderly-friendly.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: For lower-income households, we will continue to improve our public rental options.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We are also reviewing our schemes to better meet the needs of families who need to move or switch to a bigger flat when they have more children.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Senior Minister of State Sun and Senior Parliamentary Secretary Harun will share more.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Members have also asked for updates on our plans to support another group of Singaporeans – our singles.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We have made some moves to improve the housing options for singles in recent years.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: With the introduction of the new flat classification framework in 2024, first-timer singles can now buy BTO flats island-wide and not only in non-mature estates.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Since then, singles have booked flats in towns like Clementi, Bedok, Ang Mo Kio and Kallang-Whampoa for the first time.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Last year, we also extended priority access under the Family Care Scheme to singles when they apply for a new flat to live with or near their parents.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The Government is looking at increasing the income ceiling for all buyers and lowering the eligibility age for singles to buy HDB flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We are also reviewing our schemes to better meet the needs of other groups of singles, such as those who may wish to buy a bigger flat together with their family members.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: But to do more for our singles and also for other groups of flat buyers, HDB will need to build more flats to ensure supply is adequate to meet higher demand.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We will also increase the 2-room Flexi supply by almost 50% from 2026 to 2028 to meet growing demand from seniors and singles.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This includes pressing on with the efforts to inject new housing in older towns.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The first is the Pearl's Hill neighbourhood in Outram, close to the central business district.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: With the additional subsidies for Plus and Prime flats under the new flat classification framework, we are able to offer different groups of buyers affordable public housing in very attractive locations.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We also provide housing grants of up to $120,000 for eligible first-timer families, which further reduces the amount they need to pay for their flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: After more than 40 years, we will be building public housing at Pearl's Hill.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The new public housing development will be located right next to Outram Park MRT station, at the foothills of Pearl's Hill City Park.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It will comprise 2-room Flexi, 3-room and 4-room BTO flats as well as public rental flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Drawing from the nearby Chinatown heritage, the design concept is inspired by "山水画", like a Chinese painting depicting mountains and flowing rivers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Our vision is for residents to live amidst the tranquillity of Pearl's Hill, while remaining connected to the dynamic energy of the city.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: At the base level of this new development, residents and the public can enjoy green communal spaces, akin to river plains.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Moving up, a cascading water feature will serve to manage stormwater during heavy downpours.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: A green canopy of trees will provide shade, flowing seamlessly from the nearby park.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These features will also benefit the wider Pearl's Hill neighbourhood by having seamless barrier-free access from the park to the MRT.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The residential blocks will be built with varying heights like the mountain ridges in a painting.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Within the blocks, sky gardens and terraces will offer views from different levels, allowing residents to experience the surrounding landscape from multiple vantage points.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: In line with our urban design guidelines, we will preserve a view corridor, a 40-metre-wide unobstructed line of sight between the new buildings.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Air and light will be able to flow through, ensuring that the tall buildings do not overwhelm the landscape and allowing the public to enjoy views to and from Pearl's Hill City Park.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: But 60 storeys will be more than 10 storeys taller than The Pinnacle@Duxton, which is our current tallest public housing project.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This is part of our efforts to find ways to build more public housing by intensifying land usage and building taller where possible.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Currently, most tall buildings are in the central region due to aviation height restriction requirements around our airports, such as those at Changi and Seletar.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These requirements have been in place since the 1950s and were set by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO).

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Over the last decade, Singapore worked with ICAO to change these requirements and taller buildings can now be built near airports.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This change frees up more airspace for non-aviation purposes and presents opportunities for us to intensify development in different parts of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: With these regulatory changes and our experience in Pearl's Hill, HDB will find more opportunities to build taller flats across Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We will proceed carefully and sensitively, building taller only when conditions allow.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We will also pay close attention to design and liveability.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These efforts will contribute to increasing land productivity and support our plans to continue providing a robust supply of HDB flats to meet the housing needs of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Another area where we will develop a large number of new flats is Toa Payoh.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Toa Payoh was the first town to be comprehensively planned and built from scratch in the mid-1960s.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The town has evolved over the years through efforts such as the Remaking Our Heartland programme, Neighbourhood Renewal Programme and the Silver Upgrading Programme.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We have improved connectivity and invested in major infrastructure in the area, such as the Caldecott MRT station, which is an interchange for the Thomson-East Coast and Circle Lines.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Over the past 10 years, we have added 4,500 new homes in Toa Payoh, which have brought in more younger families.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: To maintain Toa Payoh's unique character, we have kept iconic features like the dragon playground and the pedestrian mall at the town centre.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This year, HDB will be launching another BTO parcel right next to Caldecott MRT station.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The development will include a new neighbourhood park with spaces for residents to exercise, play, rest and enjoy therapeutic activities as well as commercial facilities such as a food court and fast-food restaurant, a supermarket, retail shops and a childcare centre.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: An Active Ageing Centre will be established to cater to our Community Care Apartment residents and other seniors from the community.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: As residents move in a few years later, other major developments in the vicinity will be completed.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This includes the North-South Corridor underground works, which will allow us to progressively transform the surface streets and strengthen the connections between Toa Payoh West and its surrounding areas.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: To the west, wider footpaths across Thomson Road and Lornie Road will create safer and more pleasant crossings for pedestrians.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Residents will be able to cycle or walk and enjoy nature at MacRitchie Reservoir just a short distance away.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: To the east, residents will be able to easily access the rest of Toa Payoh, including the upcoming Toa Payoh Integrated Development (Sports and Lifestyle Hub), which is expected to be completed by 2030, hopefully earlier.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Residents can enjoy Toa Payoh Integrated Development's sport facilities as well as a rejuvenated Toa Payoh town park, library and polyclinic.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: A new mixed-use development with private residential units, retail and community uses will also be built at the Caldecott site.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This will include a shopping centre, which will provide residents with more retail and dining options.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It will be similar in scale as Woodleigh Mall in Bidadari.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These will be mostly for public housing as well as some private condominiums, including the mixed-use development that I just mentioned.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: In Toa Payoh West, these homes will be integrated into the lush, hilly terrain, some with views of MacRitchie Reservoir.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We will build more neighbourhood parks, so residents can enjoy urban living integrated with nature.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We will also ensure sufficient amenities, such as schools, community spaces and transport options.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Chairman, Mr Pritam Singh has suggested to remove the income ceiling for HDB BTO flats entirely and impose additional restrictions on the buyers who exceed the income threshold.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: With the New Flat Classification framework, the income ceiling is still necessary to ensure that highly subsidised BTO flats are prioritised for those who are earning below the income ceiling.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This is because higher income earners can have access to other housing options.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: And as Mr Ang Wei Neng and Mr Cai Yinzhou noted, we are reviewing the income ceiling for BTO flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: As a higher income ceiling will result in more people applying, we will need to ensure that the supply is adequate before we make these changes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: So, I would like to invite Mr Singh to perhaps file a Parliamentary Question and we will provide him with the information.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: But, Sir, allow me to clarify that the number of appeals may not fully represent the potential increase in the demand for BTO flats if we were to remove the income ceiling entirely.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: So, this is something that I think we will need to study carefully.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We need to understand what are the trade-offs, including that after you remove the income ceiling, there will be additional competition coming from those who have higher income, who have exceeded the income thresholds, for the buyers whose income fall below the income eligibility threshold.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: So, this is something that I think we need to study carefully.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I understand where Mr Singh is coming from and there are some trade-offs and I think it is a move that we will have to look at the trade-offs carefully.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I have said previously that the VERS package should be fair to existing flat owners and also sustainable for future generations.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I have also shared that we aim to flesh out as much of the VERS policy framework as possible in this term of Government.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: When we are ready with our initial proposals, MND and HDB will engage Singaporeans to take in further views and feedback before we firm up the policy.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: In the meantime, residents in our older public estates can continue to benefit from existing upgrading programmes, like the Neighbourhood Renewal Programme and the Silver Upgrading Programme.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Mr Cai Yinzhou asked about HIP and if we can share more details about how HIP II will meet residents’ changing needs as their estates age.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Flat owners can look forward to a second round of upgrading works via HIP II when their flats reach the 60- to 70-year mark.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: HIP II will be more extensive than the current HIP, and will make use of new technologies, like microwave scanning, to ensure that our ageing estates are well maintained and liveable.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We will share more about the scheme in due course.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Liang also asked for more funding support for Town Councils to cope with rising costs and the challenges posed by ageing infrastructure, such as water seepage.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Singh asked about expanding the facade repairs co-payment scheme, so that the Government and Town Councils co-fund repairs for water seepage from block facades.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The Government provides funding support to assist Town Councils with their various areas of responsibility.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Liang spoke about some of these earlier.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These include estate maintenance and improvement projects, lift maintenance and building façade repairs to ensure public safety.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Such funding support is extended to all Town Councils.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: For water seepage-related cases which require façade repairs to address public safety concerns, HDB currently co-funds repairs under the Façade Repairs Co-Payment Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: HDB also works closely with Town Councils to deal with more complex cases of water seepage by providing technical guidance.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We will review Mr Singh’s suggestion, but as different cases may have their unique considerations, we will need to assess each case on its own merits.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Residents contribute through their S&CC, and Town Councils play an important role to ensure that maintenance and other services are delivered in a cost-efficient manner, with Government providing grants and technical support to complement these efforts.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I think this is the approach that we will continue to take.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It is a shared responsibility and therefore, all the different parties will need to contribute to achieving the positive outcomes for our residents.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: And this is more than 50% higher than the number of units launched for sale in 2024 and broadly similar to 2025.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We are also studying how to enhance the liveability of private residential estates.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Many private estate residents, including our seniors, have shared their concerns about rising maintenance costs and ageing facilities, especially in older estates.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We are looking into how the Government can provide some co-funding support for our private estate in key upgrading works, particularly where it concerns safety and liveability.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It will require a combination of carrots and sticks.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Minister Indranee will share more about our plans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We have seen moderation in the HDB resale and private housing markets in recent months.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This follows from our strong pipeline of BTO flats as well as the four rounds of cooling measures we rolled out over the last few years.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The measures have taken time to work their way through the market, and we are starting to see some initial results.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We are watching the market closely and stand ready to adjust our measures, bearing in mind that more flats will reach their MOP in the next few years, thereby increasing the supply of resale flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng and Mr Cai Yinzhou asked about the 15-month wait-out period for private property owners to purchase resale flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This applies to the private property owners who are below the age of 55 or for those who are above the age of 55 if they were to buy 5-room and larger flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I want to assure the Members that we will remove this restriction when conditions allow.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: In the meantime, HDB will continue to consider appeals from households facing their own set of circumstances, and this will be done on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: In the private residential property market, for 2025, we similarly saw the smallest increase in prices since 2020.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Louis Chua asked about how we can continue to ensure affordability for ECs.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Similar points have been raised by others in this House previously, including Mr Henry Kwek and Mr Murali Pillai.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: ECs were introduced to provide an option for higher-income Singaporeans who aspire to own private housing.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: EC developments are strata-titled and have design features and facilities similar to private condominium developments.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: ECs are therefore more comparable to private condominiums than resale flats, because resale flats are still part of public housing.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: While ECs are priced by private developers, the prices are lower than private housing as we impose initial eligibility and ownership restrictions, such as an income ceiling and a minimum occupation period.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Eligible EC buyers can also benefit from a CPF Housing Grant of up to $30,000.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We are reviewing the policy and will consider your suggestions as part of the review.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The second priority for MND is to transform our Built Environment (BE) sector to improve productivity and to reduce costs, time and manpower.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This is not a new priority, but we need to give it a renewed focus and stronger push.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We have set out ambitious plans for Singapore’s development as an endearing home and global city; from providing a robust supply of public and private housing to laying the foundations for Singapore’s next bound of economic development – constructing Changi Airport Terminal 5 and Tuas Port, building new economic districts, expanding our rail network, and many more.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These are long-term projects that will benefit many generations of Singaporeans and have lasting impact for decades to come.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: To turn these plans into reality, our BE sector needs to be ready for the challenge.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Henry Kwek and Ms Lee Hui Ying spoke about this.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: For example, how do we benefit from advances in technology to save time, costs and manpower?

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: AI and robotics can transform construction into a fast, smart and highly automated process, where software systems help designers to optimise sub-components that can be constructed by 3D printers in days rather than months.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Autonomous robots could be used to construct buildings, monitored in real-time for delays and safety by drones.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: And we can have safer worksites, lower costs, reduced wastage and better-quality buildings delivered faster than before, at better value to the owners and occupants.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This will also open up more exciting and meaningful job opportunities for Singaporeans, jobs which are no longer perceived to be “dusty, dirty and dangerous” but “dynamic, decarbonised and digitalised”.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: So, it is still three “Ds”, but a different set of three “Ds”, with strong growth prospects and career development pathways.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: To achieve this, I announced last month that we have set up an Action Team to improve BE productivity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The team comprises representatives from Government agencies and the industry and will develop measures to help the industry achieve savings in time, costs and manpower.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It will focus on three areas: scaling up the adoption of productive technologies and progressive practices; reviewing our regulatory approach to reduce regulatory compliance burden, support innovation and improve procurement and contracting practices; and supporting an enabling ecosystem for the industry to reap system-level synergies and address industry-wide challenges.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We will also continue to focus on upskilling and investing in our architects, engineers, quantity surveyors, project managers and many more, because people are at the heart of the BE sector.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: On our part, the Government will continue to review our policies, rules and processes to keep regulatory burden and compliance costs as low as possible.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Minister Indranee will share more in her speech.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We plan to build more homes, new economic districts, more transport connections and nodes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: But as a small island city-state, our land supply is constrained.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: So, we have to be creative and think hard about how to optimise the use of every parcel of land.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: One way is to rejuvenate our older estates to ensure that they remain liveable and vibrant, and at the same time we can intensify how the land is used.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We will have to navigate these trade-offs carefully, to develop Singapore sustainably for future generations.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Minister of State Alvin Tan will share more about how we are doing so.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Chairman, over the past six decades, Singaporeans have transformed our small island into a thriving global city and endearing home.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We must continue to build on our fundamentals, while looking ahead to the future with confidence and optimism.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: For our homebuyers and residents, we will keep up a robust supply of private and public housing, and we will create common spaces where we can build strong communities.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: To our industry partners, we will work with you to grow a stronger, more productive and more resilient BE sector.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: One which can also provide many good jobs for our people.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: And for younger Singaporeans and our future generations, we will continue to plan boldly and build sustainably for the longer term, so that we leave behind a better future for you than what we have inherited from our forefathers.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Members for their cuts.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Transforming the BE sector and strengthening the pipeline of BE professionals, governance, liveability and maintenance of strata developments, and improving accessibility of buildings.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have many exciting plans for our city.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Last December, we gazetted our Master Plan, which lays out the blueprint for the development of Singapore over the next 10 to 15 years.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will expand our rail network by over 100 kilometres and lay out over 50 kilometres of new park connectors by the 2030s, to create a more connected, sustainable and liveable Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Hence, young people who are looking for future careers with strong growth prospects and rewarding career development pathways with meaning and purpose should consider the BE sector.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our distinctive city skyline, our iconic buildings like Jewel and the Marina Bay Sands, every HDB flat housing a family, every MRT station connecting communities, every school nurturing the next generation – are all legacies of the BE professionals whose work has left a lasting impact on our people's lives.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And in a time of climate change, it is the BE professionals who will be the vanguard in the battle for sustainability.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In 2024, we set up the Taskforce for Architectural and Engineering Consultants, co-chaired by Mr Chaly Mah, Chairman of the Surbana Jurong Group and myself.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Last year, the Taskforce completed its work and launched a suite of 11 recommendations to strengthen the BE pipeline and its transformation.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, I am pleased to share the strong industry response and tangible progress achieved to date.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Its key features include Interactive Mentorship, Structured Learning, Purposeful Tasks, Innovative Solutions and Rewarding Experience – hence, "INSPIRE".

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Under INSPIRE, the internships will be extended to minimally 30 weeks and are structured to help interns develop key technical and soft skills.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The internship can be done over multiple stints with the same firm without delaying graduation timelines.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Dedicated mentors will guide interns and provide advice in areas such as career development and excelling in the workplace.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Firms like PH Consulting, DCA Architects, and Aedas, have committed to the programme.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Surbana Jurong Group has onboarded six interns who have started their internships since January 2026.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Among them is Charlotte Chan, a third-year civil engineering student from the Nanyang Technological University.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: She opted for the 30-week INSPIRE internship rather than the standard 20-week internship.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Charlotte was motivated by the opportunity to contribute more to projects and deepen her learning experience.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: She has expressed appreciation for her supervisor's dedicated mentorship and the higher allowance that INSPIRE interns receive.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The number of participating firms is expected to grow as more industry players recognise the value of nurturing interns with strong workforce readiness.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As the INSPIRE internship will deepen skills acquisition, the Professional Engineers Board (PEB) and the Board of Architects (BOA) will recognise this pre-graduation experience as qualifying practical experience towards professional registration.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Beyond fresh graduates, the PEB and BOA will recognise relevant business and leadership related courses as part of the Continuing Professional Development framework to encourage our practising professionals to strengthen business capabilities and acumen.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Industry branding efforts are also showing early results.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Through the BuildSG Marketing Campaign, we worked closely with industry leaders, trade association and chambers, working professionals, students, and the public to position the sector as a career of choice.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Over the past academic year, there has been an increase in students applying for and enrolling in architecture and civil engineering courses.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will press on with efforts to attract our fair share of the best and brightest to join the BE sector.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For our next phase, we will work on uplifting the quantity surveying profession.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Quantity surveyors (QSes), sit at the intersection of engineering, finance and law, and they play critical roles in the smooth delivery of projects.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Their expertise lies in managing contracts and project costs within the consultant team.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As QSes' work will be increasingly automated with technology, the QS profession will need to redefine its role and provide more value-added services to stay relevant.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This requires the QS profession to build new competencies, master new technologies and strengthen the talent pipeline.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have established a workgroup to look into this, comprising QS representatives, service buyers, the institutes of higher learning (IHL), and relevant agencies.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The QS workgroup will consult stakeholders widely and make recommendations to uplift and future-proof the QS profession.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I encourage everyone to share your feedback and suggestions with us.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Henry Kwek asked how we intend to increase productivity and be more pro-enterprise for the BE sector, and Ms Lee Hui Ying asked about our long-term plans to support the growth of the construction industry through infrastructure, manpower and talent.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These are pertinent questions that highlight the need for the continued transformation of the BE sector.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Members also raised valid concerns regarding growing cost pressures and supply chain volatility.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We hear your concerns and are taking several steps to address them.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, we recognise that contractors need greater visibility of key cost drivers to plan effectively.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government is working closely across agencies to improve forward projections and coordination for critical resources, including soil disposal capacity and dormitory supply.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Additionally, we will explore how to provide the industry with more regular updates on the timeline of major infrastructure projects to support more informed project planning decisions.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Minister Chee earlier shared about our plans to help the wider BE sector save time, cost and manpower through the Action Team to improve BE productivity.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, we have enhanced our procurement and regulatory frameworks.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This enables fairer risk allocations and allows consultants to be better insured against professional liabilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We hear Ms Lee Hui Ying's suggestion to review the liability framework for contractors, to ensure robust safety standards while allowing the industry to operate productively.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: BCA will continue to work closely with contractors and refresh our policies taking into consideration industry feedback.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, we have launched the Built Environment Culture of Appreciation, Respect and Empathy (BE CARE) Charter.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Charter outlines best practices to develop more collaborative relationships amongst project teams and strengthen workplace well-being.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Arup Singapore is a good example of how the BE CARE spirit can be translated in practical actions.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Arup promotes a culture where employees feel safe to speak up and raise concerns.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It has put in place frameworks for staff to escalate issues or seek support from the leadership and people team, including anonymous hotline and whistleblower channels.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For project meetings, Arup practises smart communication by planning clear meeting agendas and involving only relevant participants.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Staff also respect one another's rest periods by scheduling after-hours emails and having structured handovers before leave days.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These are simple practices but make a difference in creating a culture that supports staff well-being.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I encourage more firms to come onboard to collectively improve the BE workplace culture.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Third, we are making progress in leveraging technology.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Architectural firms are embracing AI to transform work processes.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: DP Architects has founded a technology startup, Spatial Intelligence for Design, which is developing AI solutions for the industry.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We encourage more firms to seize the new opportunities that arise as more technologies mature.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Interested firms may tap on the Productivity Solutions Grant or the Built Environment Technology and Capability Grant for support.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The new Productivity Solutions Grant tranche will expand support to more solutions, including AI and advanced equipment, such as robotics and automation, including remote-controlled machineries and inspection and imaging equipment, which have shown encouraging productivity gains.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Fourth, trade associations and chambers have ramped up efforts to support their member firms and drive industry transformation in various areas.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, the Singapore Institute of Architects will be developing an employment resource guide, which includes structured courseware and practical workshops for Singapore Institute of Architects member firms.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This initiative equips human resource officers with the skills to better define job roles and chart career progression pathways across the firm.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This will enable firms to attract suitable talent and better craft employment contracts as well as support employees in their career development.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These are some of the efforts to implement the taskforce's recommendations to transform the BE sector.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Moving ahead, we look forward to higher participation by even more stakeholders and greater momentum.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government will also continue to review our policies in partnership with the industry to further improve BE efficiency and productivity.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Next, let me turn to our plans to improve governance, liveability and maintenance in condominiums and other strata developments.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As strata developments age, MCSTs and unit owners have expressed concerns about rising maintenance costs, ageing facilities and the challenges of collective decision-making to make improvements.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, many MCSTs only start collecting funds for lift replacement when the ageing lifts start to experience wear and tear and parts become obsolete.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If the MCSTs do not have sufficient sinking funds, they will need to collect special levies from unit owners, which may not be an insignificant sum and for which the owners may not be prepared.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This can be avoided if the MCSTs start building up the funds earlier.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To have some oversight over MCSTs' financial planning, we are exploring requiring MCSTs to submit and publish key information about their budgets and finances in a standard format.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This would make it easier for unit owners and prospective buyers to understand and track the financial health and sinking fund adequacy of the MCSTs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On strengthening governance, we are studying measures to prevent gaming of voting systems.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have received feedback on situations where a small group collects many proxy votes and controls decisions in the development.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This may not necessarily reflect the best interests of the majority of owners.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are therefore considering limiting the percentage of total proxies which can be held by each household and ensuring that council members undergo proper training.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These changes aim to make estate management fairer and more efficient.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: BCA has been engaging strata stakeholders on some of these proposed amendments since June 2025 through platforms such as focus group discussions.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We strongly encourage residents of strata developments to provide your feedback.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This review will strengthen our strata management framework to ensure that private residential developments remain well-maintained, accessible and liveable.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are studying measures to improve the safety and accessibility of our buildings and infrastructure.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: One area that we are looking into is enhancing the safety of older lifts and escalators.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are reviewing measures to ensure that ageing lifts and escalators keep pace with modern safety standards such as through the inclusion of features that regulate their speed and movement.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are also exploring providing co-funding support for select essential safety features to eligible private building owners and operators.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As our population ages, our accessibility needs will increase.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Many buildings were built in the earlier years when accessibility standards were less well developed.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Introduced in 2007, the Accessibility Fund provides co-funding to encourage private building owners to upgrade their properties with accessibility and universal design features.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: MND is reviewing potential enhancements to the Accessibility Fund to better support our seniors, persons with disabilities and families to navigate their living environment more safely, including in private developments.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Currently, active ageing and dementia-friendly features are not eligible for funding under the Accessibility Fund.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These enhancements aim to create living spaces that enable seniors to stay mobile and physically active and continue living comfortably in familiar surroundings as they age.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To encourage more buildings to pursue upgrades in line with the latest accessibility codes, we are also exploring expanding the Accessibility Fund eligibility to include more private buildings beyond those built before the implementation of the 1990 and 2013 Code on Accessibility.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To boost participation and reduce the cost for private developments, we are also reviewing the amount of co-funding support.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The initiatives I have outlined today reflect our unwavering commitment to build a better Singapore for all generations, present and future.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As we build tomorrow's Singapore together, we do so with confidence that our investments today will create a built environment that is world-class in standards and deeply rooted in our values of inclusivity, safety and excellence.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is how we ensure that Singapore remains a place every citizen will be proud to call home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Members for their questions and suggestions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Housing is a deeply personal issue because housing needs vary across households and life stages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, couples thinking about settling down and starting a family will have different needs from seniors planning ahead for retirement and independent living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We want to ensure that our housing policies and options cater to the diverse needs of various groups across different life stages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Many young couples apply for a BTO flat as their first home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As Mr Foo Cexiang pointed out, affordability and accessibility are top concerns for these young couples.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is understandable since housing is likely one of their most significant financial commitments at this stage of their life journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Securing a home may feel daunting for those who have just started working or if you have heard stories of people who applied many times but were unable to secure a flat.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We understand these concerns, which is why we will continue to support our young couples in your homeownership journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: First, as Minister Chee mentioned in his speech, we will maintain a strong supply of BTO flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the most recent BTO sales exercise just last month, the median application rate for first-timer families applying for 3-room and bigger flats was 0.9 times.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For young couples who want to secure a flat earlier, we encourage you to consider applying for a less competitive project.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our BTO flats are priced with significant market discounts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Even for young couples just starting out in your careers, it is likely that you will be able to make your monthly HDB housing repayments with little or no cash outlay.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This was the case for nine out of 10 first-timer families who collected keys to their BTO flats in 2025.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For first-timer young couples, the Staggered Downpayment Scheme reduces the initial downpayment to as low as 5% of the flat price.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Couples where one party is in or freshly out of school or National Service can apply to defer their income assessment for the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant and an HDB housing loan until just before key collection and potentially have their initial downpayment further reduced to 2.5% of the flat price.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Third, for eligible families who have booked a flat and require temporary housing while awaiting flat completion, we support them through subsidised rental via the Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme (PPHS).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Since 2021, we have significantly ramped up PPHS supply from about 800 units to more than 4,000 today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Cai Yinzhou asked about raising the PPHS income ceiling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Today, the PPHS income ceiling is set at $7,000 to better target support at families who are less able to afford renting a flat from the open market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Collectively, these measures demonstrate our commitment to support young couples in purchasing their first home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As families settle in and grow, their housing needs may change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Foo Cexiang and Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin asked how we are supporting the needs of larger families.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Today, families with three or more children can benefit from the Third Child Priority Scheme (TCPS).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The scheme is open to both first- and second-timer households.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Eligible families receive priority allocation for up to 5% of flats sold in the BTO and Sale of Balance Flats (SBF) exercises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: TCPS has been quite popular with application rates of around five times for 5-room and bigger flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I am pleased to share that we will enhance the TCPS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This will allow more eligible families to secure a flat.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These changes will take effect from the June 2026 sales exercise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Furthermore, to support larger families, we will work towards increasing the supply of bigger flats in the longer term.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is part of our strategy to sustain a robust supply of HDB flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We recognise that there will be applicants who face specific and unique challenges, such as single unwed parents, as mentioned by Mr Cai Yinzhou and Mr Foo Cexiang or those with widowed or divorced parents, as mentioned by Ms Sylvia Lim.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr David Hoe also earlier suggested greater flexibility on the Minimum Occupation Period for families who have grown and need bigger flats with more space.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For such cases, we will consider their extenuating circumstances and are prepared to exercise flexibility on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Beyond flat affordability and accessibility, we are also doing more to support residents' move-in and living experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For residents moving into new large-scale BTO estates, new amenities may take some time to become fully operational.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To improve the move-in experience, MND and HDB set up the BTO Coordination Committee comprising partner agencies like the Land Transport Authority (LTA), National Environment Agency (NEA), Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA), Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) and People's Association (PA).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the past eight months, we have had intensive discussions with grassroots advisers and identified five key areas where agencies will better support residents moving into new large-scale BTO estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: First, bus operations in new housing estates are usually introduced when there is a critical mass of residents, about three months after the first residents have collected their keys.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have heard feedback that the first batch of residents need earlier transport connectivity to help in their moving-in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These bus services will be accessible from a bus stop within walking distance of the BTOs and connect residents to amenities and transport nodes such as bus interchanges or MRT stations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In cases where a regular service cannot commence immediately, agencies will look at interim shuttle bus services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Second, residents want some access to cooked food and groceries when they move in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Currently, shop operators who rent from HDB commence operations about nine months after the first batch of residents collect their keys, as this is when they assess that there are enough residents to support their business viability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: HDB will introduce three initiatives to support shop operators so that residents can enjoy earlier access to cooked food and groceries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: First, HDB has relooked construction timelines and will bring forward the completion of shops as close as possible to the first batch of key collection.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: HDB will also pre-build outdoor refreshment areas, instead of coffee shop operators having to do so themselves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This will reap time savings of up to eight months and provide cost savings for operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Similarly, for coffee shops, their rent-free period will increase from the current three months to a maximum of six months.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This will apply to shop tenders from March 2026, and shops will need to start operations early to enjoy the maximum six-month rent-free period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For the first two years of operations, HDB also staggers rents, with rent set at 80% and 90% for the first and second year respectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Shop operators can start with a smaller offering of groceries and cooked food, before ramping up to the full offering when a critical mass of residents move in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Third, the timelines for childcare centres starting operations can vary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We found that some childcare centres are ready seven months after the first batch of residents collect their keys, while others can take more than a year to be ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This can be problematic for families who have young children at the point of moving in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Moving forward, we will work closely with ECDA to better support residents with young children moving into new large-scale BTO estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: First, HDB will aim to site childcare centres in the first blocks to be completed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This better aligns the timeline for childcare centre readiness and the first batch of residents moving in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Second, HDB and ECDA will also streamline construction and handover processes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Potential childcare centre operators will be invited to view the premises as early as possible, to facilitate planning for renovation works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The fourth area is with regard to sheltered linkways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Today, HDB plans new BTO estates with a network of sheltered linkways to support residents' daily movements from within the precinct to key transport nodes nearby, such as bus stops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Where practical, linkways are also built to connect residents to amenities adjacent to the BTO estate, such as schools or neighbourhood centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Moving forward, HDB will enhance the standard for the provision of sheltered linkways in new BTOs where there are clear benefits to residents' safety and convenience, and these linkways will be built before residents move in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: However, not all linkways will be built prior to key collection as residents' walking patterns and accessibility needs may evolve after they move in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Town Councils and other agencies may also add or extend linkways progressively, factoring in residents' walking patterns and new amenities which may be introduced over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This ensures that estates remain connected in service of residents' needs over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: HDB is working with the NEA and Town Councils to step up the provision of skip tanks, which are large bins for disposing of bulky items and receptacles, such as metal cages or recycling bins, to provide convenience to residents during the initial move-in period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Since August 2025, HDB has been providing 50% co-funding to Town Councils that wish to deploy skip tanks at newly completed projects within the first year of the project's completion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to do so for projects in new large-scale BTO estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In addition, HDB will strengthen enforcement against indiscriminate dumping by renovation contractors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This includes reviewing the penalty framework to implement stiffer penalties for errant contractors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Every estate is different and there can be project-specific issues that cause some variation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: However, with the basic principles established, we can strive towards achieving these standards for new large-scale BTO estates and can improve the move-in experience for our residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are also improving the liveability of our estates through stakeholder and resident engagement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We recognise that our HDB homes are not only a roof above our heads but also a place to grow and to improve our well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In December last year, we introduced the Play Values Framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This recognises that our playgrounds are an important infrastructure and community space for our young families with children.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: With this in mind, we actively consulted early childhood and health professionals, playground specialists and parents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: More will be shared in the coming months.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Another aspect of a good living environment is convenient access to essential goods and services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Louis Chua asked about how we ensure good supply and diversity of our neighbourhood shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our usual approach is to have a Town Centre at the heart of every HDB town, to serve as the key commercial hub and provide a broad range of goods and services, such as supermarkets, food and beverage outlets and retail shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The town centre is complemented by neighbourhood centres that are distributed across the town.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In selected precincts that are located further away from the town centre and neighbourhood centres, HDB will also build precinct shops which generally include an eating house, supermarket or minimart and a few shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Most residents will be able to access commercial facilities with a food court or eating house within 400 metres from their homes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Most residents would prefer commercial facilities, such as a food court or eating houses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: When Members have identified specific HDB estates that need vending machines or hot food and which is supported by market demand and supply, HDB will discuss with Members to facilitate the process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Azhar Othman and Mr Pritam Singh raised suggestions on rental rates and transparency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Several Members including Mr Henry Kwek, Mr Ang Wei Neng, Ms Mariam Jaafar and Mr Louis Chua have made similar points in this House on 24 September 2025.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Azhar suggested that rents be monitored and adjusted by a committee, like the Public Transport Council.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Shops can have a variety of attributes, like location, layout, trade use and branding, which leads to different service offerings and therefore command different rental rates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Also, unlike public transport, each rental transaction is a distinct contractual agreement between willing landlords and tenants, where landlords and tenants take into account market dynamics before making their decision.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Public transport, on the other hand, serves the mass public and allows for fare-setting to ensure affordability and financial sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Azhar Othman and Mr Pritam Singh, like the Members before them, including Mr Henry Kwek, Mr Ang Wei Neng and Ms Mariam Jaafar, want to see reasonable and sustainable HDB shop rental rates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: First, HDB ensures a good supply of shops in every HDB estate and town.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: When there is adequate supply, tenants have a choice of where to rent, and customers have a choice of where to buy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: If rents and product prices are too expensive, both tenants and customers have a choice to go elsewhere.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Second, for shops rented out by HDB, we have introduced new measures to keep rents stable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Tenderers are thus encouraged to strike a balance between competitiveness and business sustainability when submitting their tender bids.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For HDB shop tenants facing financial difficulties, HDB will work closely to provide targeted support, where feasible, so that residents can continue to have access to affordable goods and services in their neighbourhood.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
