text: In terms of stall rents in HDB coffee shops, it is HDB's intent to enhance transparency and support a well-functioning market by making available relevant rental data to members of the public so that potential stall holders can make prudent business decisions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are exploring the feasibility of collecting and publishing other relevant rental data for HDB coffee shops, such as the rent charged by HDB for outdoor refreshment areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This rental data collected by IRAS is made available by geographical location and property type on URA's Real Estate Information System (REALIS).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are committed to publishing accurate data which will help potential shop or stall holders make their decisions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And we will consider a dedicated portal if that is necessary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: More broadly, we are also taking a whole-of-Government approach to prevent, detect and penalise money laundering activities, including through strengthening our monitoring and sensemaking mechanisms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This helps to safeguard our markets, including public and private rental markets, guarding against the impact of such illicit activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Taken together, these measures help to ensure that our residents continue to have convenient access to an affordable and diverse selection of heartland shops and services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Chairman, I will now say a few words in Mandarin, please.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: (In Mandarin):   To help the residents access quality and affordable goods and services, as well as to maintain reasonable and stable rentals, HDB will ensure that each housing estate and town has sufficient supply of shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For shops under HDB, we have other measures to maintain the stability of shop rentals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: HDB not only considers the tender price but also conducts a more comprehensive evaluation of the tender proposals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In addition, HDB has also launched the following measures in January this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In recent years, we have stepped up our efforts to make our HDB towns more liveable, inclusive and responsive to residents' needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to work with Singaporeans to build flats and neighbourhoods that they are proud to call home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Members for their questions and cuts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Building an inclusive and cohesive society has always been at the heart of Singapore's public housing story.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: As Minister Chee mentioned, I will share how we have been and will continue to strengthen housing support for the more vulnerable Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Over the years, we have been improving HDB flat designs, including for our public rental flats.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Newer rental blocks have better ventilation and natural lighting.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We have improved the layout of each unit to maximise usable space.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Rental blocks are also better integrated within each estate to facilitate access to precinct facilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: In fact, today we have rental flats in the same blocks as sold flats.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: They create more opportunities for families living in rental flats and sold flats to interact and contribute to our broader vision of building a more inclusive society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: HDB has completed eight such integrated blocks and another 36 are under construction.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: For many of our vulnerable families, the public rental scheme has been an important source of support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Mr Nazri Zakaria, Ms Nurfitrah Yahya and their four young children moved into a 2-room public rental flat in 2020.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: But agencies stepped in to lend a hand.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Their family benefitted from the ComLink+ programme, where MSF works with agencies, including HDB, to provide integrated support to families with children under 21.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Alongside this, HDB's Home Ownership Support Team reached out to Mr Nazri and Ms Nurfitrah to help them along their journey towards home ownership.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Mr Nazri and Ms Nurfitrah shared that the assistance from the Home Ownership Support Team has been invaluable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: While Mr Nazri had secured stable full-time employment as a bus driver to help his family regain their financial footing, home ownership still felt like a distant possibility initially.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: This was because the decision to purchase a home is indeed a big one.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: The Home Ownership Support Team worked through the purchase price of their possible flat options, explaining how much downpayment would be required as well as the anticipated monthly mortgage repayments.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: By breaking down the cost, the couple had better awareness of how this could fit within their budget.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: The Home Ownership Support Team then guided Mr Nazri and Ms Nurfitrah in their flat selection process and remained an important resource for the family all the way until they collected the keys to their new 4-room flat in Yishun recently.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Today, Mr Nazri and Ms Nurfitrah are happy homeowners and I was privileged enough to meet their family at their new home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: I am heartened by Mr Fadli Fawzi's support for the Government's efforts in helping lower-income families accelerate their transition to home ownership.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Indeed, Mr Nazri and Ms Nurfitrah's story is one of many.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: In 2025, more than 2,000 of our existing rental households have booked a flat and are awaiting its completion.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We have been doing even more to support rental households.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We also extended the Fresh Start Housing Scheme to first-timer ComLink+ rental families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: They are now allowed to buy a 2-room Flexi or 3-room Standard flat on a shorter lease, which will be more affordable compared to those on a 99-year lease.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: As first-timers, they are eligible for the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant up to $120,000 in lieu of the Fresh Start Housing Grant.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: These enhancements will help empower even more households to achieve home ownership.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: HDB will also continue to work with rental households individually as home ownership is a long-term financial undertaking that is best informed by understanding each family's unique circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Mr Chairman, in Malay, please. :   For many vulnerable families, HDB's rental flat scheme has been an important source of support that provides protection and relief when they face hardship.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Take Mr Nazri and his family for instance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: I met them recently when they were making preparations to celebrate Hari Raya.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: In 2020, Mr Nazri Zakaria, his wife Ms Nurfitrah Yahya and their four young children moved into a 2-room HDB rental flat.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: They benefitted from the ComLink+ programme, where MSF works with agencies, including HDB, to provide integrated support to families with children under 21 years old.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: It encompasses assistance, such as in employment, education and housing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Things improved further when HDB's Home Ownership Support Team reached out to them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: The Home Ownership Support Team guided them to examine their home purchase budget and flat options and prepared a clear plan towards home ownership.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Through stable employment, joint efforts and consistent savings, Mr Nazri and Ms Nurfitrah, are now proud owners of a new 4-room flat in Yishun.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Their journey was not easy, but it was made easier with strong and continuous support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Throughout 2025, more than 2,000 HDB rental households have already booked HDB flats and are waiting for their completion.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We are expanding our efforts to support HDB rental households.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Additionally, the Fresh Start Housing Scheme was also extended to First-Timer ComLink+ rental families, enabling them to buy a 2-room Flexi or 3-room Standard flat on a shorter lease.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: These measures will give opportunities to more HDB rental families to achieve their dream of owning a home and therefore improve their family's well-being. : While most of our rental households are families, a substantial 40% are singles.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Under the Joint Singles Scheme, single applicants must find co-applicants before they apply.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: That is why we introduced the Joint Singles Scheme Operator Run (JSS-OR) pilot in 2021.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Under the JSS-OR, applicants can apply individually and the social service agency that is appointed as the operator will help them to identify a suitable flatmate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Mr Lee Chwee San is one such applicant.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: He applied alone back in 2022 and New Hope Community Services, the operator for the Bukit Batok JSS-OR site, helped him to find a suitable flatmate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: The operator also helps to manage tenancy matters, mediates among tenants where necessary and organises activities to bring tenants together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: This has made a difference for Mr Lee, whom I met recently.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: He had attended a lohei session organised by New Hope and shared that such activities, which also include games sessions and other festive celebrations, were welcome opportunities to interact and bond with other tenants in the block.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We further expanded options with the Single Room Shared Facilities (SRSF) pilot in 2024.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Under SRSF, tenants have individual bedrooms but access to shared facilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Both pilots cater to different preferences and both have received positive feedback.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: That is why we launched the first purpose-built SRSF block in October last year and will scale up both typologies in the coming years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Another group that we are paying increasingly close attention to is our seniors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: As Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin highlighted, your housing needs will evolve as you age.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Some seniors want to monetise their flat, either by renting their flat out or by selling part of the remaining lease of their flat back to HDB.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Others may prefer right-sizing to a smaller flat, notwithstanding the good memories of their current home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: With a smaller flat, maintenance is easier and the proceeds can supplement their retirement needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: These are personal decisions and we will support Singaporeans regardless of the option they choose.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: For those who prefer to age in place, you can sell part of your flat's remaining lease to HDB under the LBS.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: The proceeds will be used to top up your CPF Retirement Account and provide you with monthly lifelong payouts under CPF LIFE.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: LBS also provides owners with up to $30,000 in cash bonus.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Alternatively, you can right-size to a smaller flat and use the sales proceeds to support your retirement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: For instance, seniors can consider applying for a new 2-room Flexi flat from HDB or right-sizing to a Community Care Apartment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: A Community Care Apartment integrates housing with care services and comes with preinstalled fittings and senior-friendly designs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: The next one is in Toa Payoh later this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We will continue launching more Community Care Apartments across various towns, depending on the need.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: But there is a limit to how many Community Care Apartments we can build.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: That is why we are also doing more to make our living environment more senior-friendly and ensure that our seniors can age in place comfortably.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Mr Henry Kwek and Mr Liang Eng Hwa will be pleased to hear that agencies are working together to roll out Age Well Neighbourhoods, starting with the first one in Toa Payoh.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: In each Age Well Neighbourhood, we will improve access to healthcare services and upgrade senior-friendly amenities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: This will add to the housing and care options available for seniors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We will continue to review and refine these options for seniors as we go along.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We are also heartened to hear Mr Cai Yinzhou's interest in senior-friendly fittings for residents to age in place.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Even if you are not in an Age Well Neighbourhood, you can still benefit from the many improvements through our upgrading programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: These include the Neighbourhood Renewal Programme and Silver Upgrading Programme for HDB precincts and our Estate Upgrading Programme for private estates.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Four precincts in Chong Boon will be the first to benefit from the Silver Upgrading Programme when the works are complete later this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: By next year, works will complete for another 12 precincts in Ang Mo Kio, Bukit Merah and Toa Payoh.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Mr Fadli Fawzi asked about schemes for improvements within the flat to enable seniors to live more comfortably and securely.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Seniors can tap on the EASE to receive subsidies to install items that improve mobility and safety.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: This is offered as part of HIP and EASE (Direct Application).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: From April this year, private estates can also benefit from EASE (Private).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Home Fire Alarm Device installation is also offered under EASE and in flats that have fire-rated doors installed under HIP.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: On fall detection, HDB partners commercial vendors to offer optional fall detection packages that residents living in sold flats may subscribe to.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: The Ministry of Health will also roll out the enhanced Home Personal Care service, which includes 24/7 technology-enabled monitoring to detect falls and incidents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng and Mr Dennis Tan asked about our LUP.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Over the years, HDB has piloted and adopted various solutions to bring direct lift access to more blocks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Residents living in these blocks will be informed in due course.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: For residents living in blocks without direct lift access, including those in segmented flats, we have enhanced the Lift Access Housing Grant last year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: HDB continues to explore new ways to bring direct life access to the remaining blocks, such as working with research institutes to develop and test out new solutions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Earlier this year, HDB also called for proposals under the HDB Cool Ideas Enterprise.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: This is a platform that provides enterprises with funding support, mentorship and access to testbed facilities to co-develop solutions that improve the HDB living environment and residents' quality of life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: I would also like to address Mr Dennis Tan's point that his resident at Block 832 did not know that their flat did not have the same floor direct lift access at the point of purchase.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: If the resident bought the flat directly from HDB, the relevant information would have been provided in the HDB sales brochure at the time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: If the resident bought the flat from the resale market, whether a flat has direct lift access is an observable physical feature of the property.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: On offering LUP to all blocks, regardless of cost, I hope Mr Tan appreciates that the Government needs to ensure public funds are spent prudently.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: HDB will continue to explore new technologies to provide direct lift access to remaining blocks where feasible.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We will do our best to cover as many blocks as possible.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: However, where the cost of providing direct lift access is too high, it is more prudent for the flat owner to move to another unit in the neighbourhood with lift access, using the Lift Access Housing Grant, which we enhanced last year to $80,000.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Mr Chairman, Singapore's public housing landscape is constantly evolving and we will do our best to meet the diverse needs of every Singaporean.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Whether you need a place to stay as you navigate life's difficult challenges, or whether you have retired and want to age gracefully in place, we are here to support you.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, I have spoken in this Chamber about how we must thoughtfully steward the little we have been endowed with.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And this means being aware and upfront of the trade-offs with our people as we build homes, schools and hospitals, connectivity nodes for them, and also safeguard our green and blue spaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It also means taking care of our animals, while managing human animal conflicts when they arise.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Ms Lee Hui Ying called for stronger legislative levers to deter animal cruelty.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are indeed strengthening our animal health and welfare ecosystems.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The council will register veterinarians, accredit veterinary training programmes and set continuing education requirements.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Second, we are reviewing legislation and codes to improve animal health and welfare, and strengthen safeguards against animal cruelty and abuse.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Since 2022, we have consulted widely on the Animals and Birds Act review, to better understand how we can strengthen powers for animal disease prevention and control.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are also studying how to better deter acts of animal cruelty and abuse.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: That includes reviewing imprisonment terms, fines and disqualification orders for animal welfare offences.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I have also met with Animal Concerns Research and Education Society (ACRES) and Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (SPCA) to discuss their White Paper on this issue.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will review all suggestions carefully before engaging the wider public later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: There is currently no licensing scheme for these sectors and standards vary.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will consult stakeholders and the public, as we continue to raise standards and professionalism across these sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Meanwhile, we must also manage pest bird species to protect public health and public safety.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik asked how we can better manage pigeon roosting and defecation at air-conditioner ledges.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Ms Lee Hui Ying, Mr Liang Eng Hwa, Mr Ang Wei Neng and Mr Pritam Singh asked also how we can manage pigeon, myna and crow populations more effectively.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To keep pest bird populations under control, we must tackle the root cause, which is food.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We therefore work with partners to improve food waste management, enforce against illegal bird feeding and, very importantly, educate the public.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will roll this out across Singapore in phases.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: HDB is also trialling half-height netting in Punggol and Toa Payoh to prevent pigeon nesting at the air-conditioner ledges of HDB blocks.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will share HDB's findings with all Town Councils after this trial.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Pritam Singh and Ms Lee Hui Ying also asked about the safety protocols for crow shooting.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: NParks has worked with the Ministry of Home Affairs and its relevant agencies to develop strict shooting protocols.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This includes ensuring the shooting trajectory is always directed upwards, cordoning safety zones with the appropriate signages and deploying personnel to manage public access and restrict unauthorised movement during crow shooting operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will select locations based on a range of factors, including public feedback and technical feasibility of the crow shooting operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: But ultimately, in spite of everything that we are doing, we need everyone to work together, a shared responsibility.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: These small things will help keep our living environment all the more liveable for all of us.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I agree with Ms Nadia Samdin that nature is important to our long-term resilience as a city.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: That is why we are expanding our green spaces as part of our City in Nature vision.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And we are on track to building more than 25 new parks and 50 kilometres of park connectors in the next five years.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are also enhancing ecological connectivity across our island.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are planting more native trees and shrubs along roads that mimic the multi-tiered structure of forests.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: These Nature Ways help animals, like birds and butterflies, move between our nature reserves, parks and gardens.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Together with park connectors and parks, they will form broader Nature Corridors that connect habitats across our most biodiverse areas.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are also making our parks even more welcoming and accessible, like our iconic Gardens by the Bay.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Today, I am pleased to announce that Gardens by the Bay will welcome an all-new Wetlands by the Bay.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will expand our current Kingfisher Wetlands precinct, with over 600 mangrove and coastal plants that you can kayak through.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It will be three times the current area, three times the number of plants.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will also build a new canopy boardwalk over the wetlands, connecting Gardens by the Bay MRT station to key attractions within Bay South Garden.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will also build Glade Lawn, a new community green space that will host events and activities, and also serve as a place for visitors to relax and unwind.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are also starting work on a new pedestrian bridge that directly connects Bay South and Bay East Garden and we expect to complete the bridge by 2028 – so visitors do not need to go all the way across Marina Barrage to the other side.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Beyond the Gardens, we are also rejuvenating and linking 13 parks in southwestern Singapore, including three destination parks.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Today, I am happy to share some key ideas from about 2,500 responses that will shape these parks.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Many of you who joined this consultation asked for better accessibility and amenities along key stretches, such as more recreation options, restrooms and shaded areas.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: At the same time, you also told us that you wanted us to preserve the greenery and the tranquility of the parks, while adding experiences for different users So, we will explore inclusive nature-based trails connecting the southwestern parks to bring the community closer together through discovery and play.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will enhance West Coast Park's coastal charm by integrating maritime and cultural heritage elements across the park.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will also introduce new amenities, thoughtfully taking care to protect West Coast Park's tranquil nature.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For Hort Park, we will make Hort Park an even more inclusive, welcoming gardening hub, where the community can gather and participate in hands-on programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will keep Labrador Nature Park serene and natural, while adding new features to showcase its heritage and biodiversity.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, I thank park users, the community and residents for their valuable feedback, and look forward to enhancing these parks and more.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In 2014, we established Sisters' Islands Marine Park, which has become a safe haven for turtle conservation and a living gene bank for our corals.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In fact, I visited the Marine Park last year to release 76 baby hawksbill turtles that NParks had uncovered at East Coast Park.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The centre will bring together expertise across disciplines to develop local capabilities and talent, working with institutions like St John's Island National Marine Laboratory and partners across the marine community.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: NParks is partnering the National University of Singapore on the Centre and will share more details later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Chairman, we face many competing needs as we develop Singapore and we balance these needs through careful master planning, taking a long-term view informed by Singaporean's aspirations.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Minister Chee Hong Tat shared how one of MNDs key priorities is to ensure that we develop Singapore sustainably and balance our land use requirements.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: But some trade-offs will always be with us because of our limited land size and land constraints.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Even as we steward our green and blue spaces, we must also carefully steward this balance between nature and development, as Ms Nadia Samdin has urged.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I want to assure her that we take the ecological impact of planned developments seriously.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Dennis Tan again raised concerns over Serangoon Forest and the Lorong Halus bus depot and asked for baseline studies for all forested plots.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I have already addressed this in response to its Adjournment Motion in January, but I will briefly reiterate because these are important points.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We have to balance many competing needs, including for housing, education, green spaces, within our constraints, our limited land.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Tan spoke also how other countries are safeguarding and revitalising brown field sites with nature-based solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As I have said, we do not have the luxury of land and space that other countries have.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Instead, we must make do with what little we have.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: But I want to assure him at the same time that we already have a robust framework in place to balance developmental needs against conserving green spaces that all of us enjoy.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Under our Planning Act, no development can take place without planning permission.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And as part of the planning approval process, we assess a site's potential ecological and biodiversity value.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This is based on the site's current state, not its zoning.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Where an EIA is not required, agencies may still impose measures to mitigate impact.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, it is not just mitigate, as Mr Tan has said.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In many instances, it is also avoid and adapt.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Through our EIAs, we consider needs for housing, jobs and others, alongside the ecological and biodiversity impact of the proposed development.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Decisions are made only after carefully weighing these very difficult trade-offs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Henry Kwek's example of how MND officers engaged him and his residents 22, 23 times is a case in point.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This approach protects our most ecologically sensitive sites while balancing against our pressing developmental needs.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Given that condominium prices and wages have risen over time, can MND share a timeframe or timeline when the income ceiling review will be concluded?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Is it in a matter of months, or is it when some threshold conditions are met?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Second question is, MND shared that we will have more bigger flats supply coming up.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Does it include 5-room flats, which I have asked earlier on?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: And third of all is, taller blocks mean higher specification lifts and stricter fire safety standards, driving up long-term maintenance cost.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Is MND prepared to help Town Councils offset the added life-cycle cost?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Chairman, Mr Kwek asked about the timing of our review of income eligibility threshold.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is something which we are actively looking at.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I am unable at this point in time to give him a concrete timeline, but certainly we will be ready to share this when the review is completed.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Second question, are we going to build more 5-room flats?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We also need to look at how we can intensify land usage by building taller through clever design, use of more integrated and mixed-use facilities to be able to squeeze out more land productivity.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Land is going to be limited in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That is something which I think all of us would agree.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But if we can improve land productivity, we are able to squeeze out more space, then, I can use that space to provide more supply to meet the needs of different groups of buyers – whether it is the singles, seniors, larger families and other groups.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Last question, taller blocks, are we going to be able to provide more support to our Town Councils?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We recognise that the costs have gone up, and we also recognise, as Mr Liang mentioned earlier in his cut, that in some areas the cost of providing those maintenance and services would be higher than the conventional method.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: He mentioned about the pneumatic waste collection system.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And there are some system level gains because you save land, but the maintenance cost in some areas could be higher because the operations are more complex.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, this is an area where I think if we can work closely with the Town Council, it is a win-win outcome.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Certainly, for taller blocks as well, there are system level gains that we derive.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But if there are going to be areas where Town Councils will have to spend more, then we have to look at it to see what we can do to ensure that it is a fair arrangement where the Government, Town Councils and also residents would all contribute to this.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: So, I would like to ask, how he sees the trajectory in the next two, three years.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Whether in the next two, three years, are we able to meet the peak demands for the BTO flats, mindful that family formations are much lower than that number?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: So, whether that trajectory is going to still be there.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: In the remaining 100 blocks, I am sure there are some blocks where some stacks of the blocks are technically very challenging to do, but another stack could be doable, is feasible to do.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Will HDB look at LUP for some blocks on a partial basis?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: At least some blocks get to be served with lift access, rather than just because one stack cannot be done, the whole block cannot get the lift upgrading.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The question to the first question is yes, we will continue with a robust supply of new BTO flats to meet the needs of buyers.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I shared earlier that there are different groups of buyers that we are trying to cater to.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If we lower the eligibility age for singles to be able to buy BTO flats, more people will be able to apply.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If we raise the income threshold, more people will be eligible to apply.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If we want to cater to more buyers who previously may be staying with their family members but now want to stay near but have their own flat, that will also lead to a higher demand for housing.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We are getting ready to be able to do that.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The second question on LUP, I take Mr Liang's point that we do not want to view this in a binary manner, that we cannot do for the whole block because some parts cannot do, so I take his point.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But I also seek the understanding of the House that in some cases, this may not be possible because the technology may not allow us to do it for that configuration or it will just simply be too expensive.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As Senior Parliamentary Secretary Harun mentioned earlier, we are using taxpayers' money, public funds.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
text: Second, what are the targets that the Ministry has set to increase the number of rental households transitioning to home ownership for each year up to 2030?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Syed Harun, are you taking that as a response?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: With regard to the question on when the income threshold was last reviewed, I do not have the information with me at this point of time.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: I invite the Member to file a Parliamentary Question if he so chooses.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: But I would like to assure the Member that when it comes to rental households, we do look at wanting to be able to support our vulnerable households as much as possible.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: It is not merely just about the rental flats but also a wraparound approach with regards to supporting them.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: Certainly, it is not about just the rental flats, but also about their ability to sustain their income in terms of employment opportunities as well as supporting the entire family, including the educational needs of their children.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: With regard to the Member's question on — sorry, can I just clarify the second question?

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
text: The second question is about targets, the target to increase the transition from rental housing to home ownership.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: Why we do this is because our objective is to support as many rental households as possible to achieve home ownership so long as they are ready.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: Indeed, home ownership is a long-term financial commitment.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: A family's readiness for the transition to home ownership depends on their very specific circumstances, such as employment stability and their savings.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: So, we work very closely with each rental family to assess their level of readiness for home ownership and to support them in their journey.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: In recent years, we continued to enhance this support for them to achieve so.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Could the qualifying criteria be relaxed for occupants aged 70 and above, without the need for medical certification?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Additionally, could HDB require new buyers of resale segmented flat to sign a letter of undertaking to indicate that they know that the flat is unlikely to qualify for LUP in the near future?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: We are excited about the 60-storey HDB flat that is near Pearl's Hill Terrace.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Considering our future housing needs, I agree that we should explore more options to construct higher HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Could the Minister share which HDB towns could realistically support high-rise developments of above 50 storeys?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: The last clarification is about pest, wild birds.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Is MND satisfied with the current resources to deal with the annual 22,000 cases on pest birds, would MND be prepared to add more resources to combat pest birds, including intensified efforts to control food waste and food for feeding of the birds?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: Chairman, I will take the question on the Lift Access Housing Grant.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: As far as the Lift Access Housing Grant is concerned, it is meant for citizen households with members who have medical conditions or mobility issues and who need to urgently buy another flat with direct lift access.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: Where there is a doctor who can certify that this individual has an illness or conditions which affect his mobility, among other criteria of the Lift Access Housing Grant, then that is something that we will consider for that individual.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Minister Chee, are you going to respond to the two other clarifications from Mr Ang?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Chairman, the first question about 60 storeys, I think it is a bit too early for us to pinpoint which towns we are going to be able to do this, besides the one at Pearl's Hill that I just announced.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But certainly, as I said in my speech, where we can, where possible, we would like to do so.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Because this is a way to be able to increase the number of units, making better use of the limited land that we have and create more space.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: On wild birds, I thank Mr Ang for his support.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As Minister of State Tan mentioned earlier, this requires a whole-of-society effort.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We cannot solve the problem with just adding more and more enforcement officers or pest control teams, whether NParks or contractors.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That is something that we will certainly do to make sure that they are adequately resourced to do their work, but we cannot just do that alone because we also need the other measures to work together as a package.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For example, as Senior Minister of State Tan said earlier, please do not feed the birds.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That is something which will help a lot.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It takes a whole-of-society effort for us to do this and keep our environment safe and pleasant for everyone.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Just a few very quick clarifications and questions.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: First, on the matter of lower eligibility age for singles who want to purchase BTO flats.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I believe that is what the Minister shared MND was looking into, but please correct me if I am wrong.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: At the same time, I heard the Minister mention earlier that the median application rate for singles is still high, but he did not give a number.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: However, I believe he gave a number – 2.6 times for first- and second-timers.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, I appreciate if the Minister could share what the median application rate currently for singles is.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: At the same time, in view of the review with regard to the lower eligibility age for singles, because it is a limited window for those individuals vis-à-vis their age, when will MND confirm the new age eligibility criteria for singles?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The second point is on my cut on income eligibility thresholds, to remove the ceiling.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Just to be clear, it is not a call to remove the ceiling carte blanche; there are encumbrances which I wish to stress.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I think those encumbrances can offer another option.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: It will be as good as another scheme for a certain category of BTO buyers.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I said that I called on HDB to make this information in October last year.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I hope Mr Singh understands this point and I am sure he does, which is that if I lower the age before supply is adequate, we may then end up with more people entering the market to apply.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That will also affect the existing group of applicants, including the singles who are aged 35 and above.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, to avoid that, we should time this properly, do it when we are confident that we are able to meet the increase in demand from the various groups of buyers.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The second question on the removal of the income ceiling, we are of the same understanding, Mr Singh.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I did mention in my speech earlier that you are not proposing to remove it – full stop; but with certain restrictions imposed on the people who exceed the income threshold.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I did acknowledge in my speech that it is something that we have to study carefully, because there are trade-offs.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: There will be some trade-offs that we will need to make, including what Mr Dennis Tan mentioned.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If I can avoid affecting some of the areas, I would, but we do have difficult trade-offs that we need to make.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And if we prioritise providing adequate housing supply for our people as the number one priority, and if this House agrees with that, then what it means is that we have to be honest and candid about some of the trade-offs that we have to make.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Minister of State Sun Xueling, would you like to respond to the third point from Mr Pritam Singh?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Pritam Singh made a clarification on his cut and did not have a question for me, so I have nothing to add.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: The first is on blue spaces for Minister of State Alvin Tan.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: I was very excited to hear more about the new Marine Science Centre.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: Could he please clarify how will its work complement existing efforts, for example, of St John's Island National Marine Laboratory and other institutions like the Singapore Oceanarium Research and Learning Centre, holistically, and how can Singaporeans, youths and citizen scientists be involved in its work?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: Next, could he also share more on the plans for the second Marine Park's recreational spaces, and what lessons can be learnt from the first Sister Islands Marine Park?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: I also note that the second Marine Park, which includes Lazarus South and Kusu, generally have higher levels of human activity, for example, Kusu during the pilgrimage season, and Lazarus South, for example, recreational spaces and tiny homes.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: So, how will MND take this into consideration, for example, in terms of zoning and visitor management, when designating this second park, so that we can protect our habitats and minimise pressure on the environment?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: My second clarification is for Singapore Parliamentary Secretary Syed Harun, regarding lessons learnt from the SRSF and JSS-OR pilots, including in Ang Mo Kio, where I serve.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: For example, some who work as delivery riders have asked if there can be motorcycle lots provided, and also, as there are residents who have certain health and well-being challenges, can MND look at centralising more services beyond the example given, which was New Hope, who already does a very good job, I should add.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: My last question is just for further help on supporting divorcees, as I asked in my cut.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Minister of State Alvin Tan, would you like to respond?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: First of all, I wanted to thank Ms Nadia Samdin for her work with the Friends of Marine Park, and that is why she is very interested in this.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For the second Marine Park, the intent is to safeguard the ecologically significant habitats around the area, and also to enhance the existing biodiversity with the existing ones on Sisters' Island.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The intent is also to provide spaces for recreation, for research, for outreach and for education.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In this regard, the Friends of Marine Park stakeholders are very important, together with Youth Stewards for Nature, as well as other researchers, outreach, policy groups.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: They form our key stakeholder group for us to look into addressing and also enhancing many of these features for the second Marine Park.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We will then also review any of these compatible features that we can put in after taking into consideration their feedback.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: With regards to the Marine Science Centre, it is a nationally coordinated research programme.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, the new Marine Science Centre will in fact work with the Oceanarium and others to coordinate research about marine science capabilities and biodiversity.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: It will provide a unique strategic vision across all of these different stakeholders and critically involve youths, Government stakeholders, industry researchers, universities, building talent so that we can build a good talent source to research into all the critical marine biology topics that are critical for our area.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: For SRSF, as I mentioned in my speech, the response and feedback have been positive.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: I think the residents have found that their preferences of having a room to themselves and then, subsequent to that, having shared common facilities, continue to be something that has been well received.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: That is precisely why we are looking to scale.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: While some of the limitations that the Member has shared are specific to the current temporary site, some of the feedback will also be taken with us, as we transit into the permanent block as part of the new features.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: We will continue to develop the space and we will continue to see how best we can improve for our public rental flats.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: I understand that the question was relating to other vulnerable groups, moving forward, the third question.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: We will continue to see where the needs are and we will continue to see how best we can align some of our policies to be able to reach out to these vulnerable groups.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: It remains our intent to make sure that we are able to support as many vulnerable groups, including the divorcees and the single-parent families.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: We will see how best we need to tweak some of the policies to support in that regard.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: Mr Chairman, with your permission, I would like to also respond to Mr Fadli Fawzi's earlier clarification.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: So, it really rings true with regard to our desire to look at the issue of each and every person and family holistically to then be able to see how best we can lean forward to support.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: The first is on the review of the EC policy – any timeline around that?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: Second is in terms of how the Minister talked about building a robust supply pipeline and given that we are now in March 2026.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I cannot give you a specific timeline.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think Mr Chua highlighted this in his cut as well – it is not so straightforward.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think Mr Kwek mentioned this as well.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I think this is something which we need to look at carefully: how do you intervene appropriately, but without fundamentally changing the nature of what the ECs are.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As I explained in my speech to Mr Chua's cut, ECs are more comparable to private condominiums.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Actually, after the 10-year period, they become exactly like a private condominium.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And you can sell to anyone, including foreigners.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Because of that, I think we need to ask ourselves as well: if you do this review, do you want to retain the fundamental nature of ECs, or do you want to actually change this?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think that is quite an important point to bear in mind.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And if you want to retain it, then what are some of the moves that we can make to improve affordability but yet maintain this feature that it is closer to or more comparable to private condominiums, rather than to resale flats and to public housing.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Private residential, same thing, I have also said this previously that if the demand remains strong, we do have some capacity that we can release.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: There are two ways to do this: we can either activate a new site and release it through the Government Land Sale programme; or we could convert some of the sites from reserve to the Government Land Sale programme, or put some new sites into reserve that the developers could trigger if the demand is strong.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, there are very various ways to do this, but whether it is public housing or private housing, it goes back to the fundamental point that I mentioned earlier – which is that in order to meet all these different demands, all these different needs, supply is key.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And supply means we have to build more.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We have to activate more pieces of land.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We have to improve land intensification, improve the design so that we are able to have more integrated mixed use.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These are all the different ways that we can increase the supply.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: The Tiong Bahru estate, consisting of pre-war and post-war buildings, has not had a lift since its establishment.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: A lot of the residents are getting older.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: As the Minister described, they would be prepared to do so.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: I think all of us face the concerns of pigeons defecating on the air-conditioning ledges; me as well.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: I look forward to the recommendations from the Punggol pilot, but I would like to ask the Ministry whether it would consider the use of audible pigeon deterrent devices, such as bio-acoustic units that use pre-recorded predator calls as part of the whole set of factors to combat this.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: The third one, the lifts in super high-rise flats.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: I think the example from The Pinnacle@Duxton would be quite instructive.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: Currently, the feedback that I receive from residents of Pinnacle is.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: One, they pay higher S&CC charges, but why does the lifts seem to break down sometimes?

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: And two, a lot of them tell me that they set aside at least 15 minutes to catch the lift, for the fear of having to wait for a long time, especially when one of the lifts is broken down.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: But the reality is that while they pay higher S&CC charges, the cost of maintaining this lift is actually more than for other typical HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: So, I think this point which the Minister made that up front, HDB, Town Council and residents will need to have good understanding is a very critical point.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: It may be better to over specify the number of lifts at the start and pay a higher price at the start, rather than having to maintain a large number of lifts that are not functioning properly in the future, over the longer term.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: So, that is just a point for me to highlight.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Mr Foo for his three points.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Certainly, we will be happy to work with him on some of the specific local challenges that he is facing with the older blocks in his constituency.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: On pigeons, we are open to considering different possible ways and we can test this out to see whether they are effective.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I do not know whether what Mr Foo describe is a workable solution or not, but I am prepared to try it, and I think we should be open-minded trying different ideas.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Black cat, white cat, as long as can catch mice, it is a good cat.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So as long as the method works, I think we should be prepared to try.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The last point about lifts is an important one.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Because as I described earlier, there are system level gains that we can derive when we build taller, but we do need to then make sure that we be fair to the Town Councils and be fair to the residents.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The experience with Pinnacle that was built quite some time ago.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think, today, we learn from that and when we design, we will bring in the latest design specifications and technology.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And also, I think we will certainly bear in mind how we support the Town Councils and the residents where we have some of these features in our estates that derive system level gains that all of us will benefit from but can impose some local level additional cost.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, if we can find a way to bridge that, then we can open up more possibilities that will be good for the country as a whole, the society as a whole.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: My first clarification is for Senior Parliamentary Secretary Dr Syed Harun.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Would the Senior Parliamentary Secretary be able to give a clearer timeline for the LUP for the 40 blocks?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: At least give an indication, for example, does HDB expect this to be carried out within the next two years or five years?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: My second clarification is for Minister of State Alvin.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Minister of State Alvin was replying regarding the part in my cut on avoid-minimise-mitigate and he was giving some examples of how the Ministry may have carried out their obligation under "avoid".

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I just want to make a clarification regarding this.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: And if I may, I would like to also go back to his remarks in the Adjournment Motion as an example for this clarification.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: And in the Adjournment Motion, in his reply, he has cited, for example and this is what is stated in my cut, the current bus depot construction at Serangoon River Forest.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: He said that, "Technical agencies have assessed that this site is not a sensitive nature area and environmental impact of the bus depot is limited.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Hence, an environmental study was not required." Regretfully, no details of this study was done, and the extent of the study was done and, hence, in my Adjournment Motion as well as in my cut.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Yes, I am going to put this as a point for Minister of State Alvin.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Perhaps you can summarise the gist of what you said in your Adjournment Motion and then apply it to the cut that you had filed today and then ask your clarification.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Chairman, so in my cut, I have asked, instead, for MND to require a mandatory baseline and functional assessment and institutionalise mandating an EIA.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: So, go directly to having a baseline study for all forested plots, regardless of whether it is primary forest or brownfield sites and have EIA for these sites, rather than to have what the procedure that was carried out in the case of the Lorong Halus bus depot.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Which political office holder would like to respond to this?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Dr Syed Harun and then Minister of State Alvin Tan.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: With regard to the clarifications from Mr Dennis Tan, I thank him for the clarifications.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: At the core of this is effectively, what do we need to steward?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And we need to steward both our green spaces as well as address our competing needs for land.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And that land, including for those in his area, that means greater connectivity in many other parts of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: It means more schools, more housing, more hospitals.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, even though we have different approaches to this, I hope that he understands the approach that MND and our agencies need to take for the interest of Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I would like very much to give as many Members who have put their hands up a chance to clarify.

speaker: The Chairman
text: The Clerks and I see Ms Lee Hui Ying, Mr Abdul Muhaimin and Ms Elysa Chen.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
text: First, is there updated timeline on the 15-month wait-out period for the sales of a private property for residents to purchase resale HDBs?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
text: Because every week, we meet residents who appeal to waive on this due to their unique and unfortunate circumstances; some with families with young children and sometimes have to sell because of failed businesses.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
text: So, I hope support will be provided to such families.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
text: Second, I echo Minister of State Alvin's strong call to not feed the birds.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
text: But unfortunately, recalcitrant illegal bird feeders still continue to do so.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
text: So, will there be strengthened enforcement against illegal feeding?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
text: And will there be plans for step-up surveillance in hotspots and more importantly, higher penalties for repeat offenders?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
text: And on crow shooting, I have asked this earlier in the cut as well, whether there are safeguards to minimise public exposure, especially to young children.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
text: Will there be advanced notification protocols in place to inform residents in advance of such shooting efforts?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
text: The Chairman: Perhaps a crisp response from a political officeholder.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Ms Lee had a question about the 15-month wait-out period.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, as I have explained earlier, we will monitor the situation in the resale market a little bit more.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Then all the previous efforts are all wasted.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I think we should persist with this a little while more, monitor the data and at an appropriate time when we are ready, let us make a move.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And in the meantime, if there are cases that require help, please do continue to appeal for your residents and we will look at each case on its own merits.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
text: I have two clarifications for Minister of State Tan.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
text: Regarding the pigeon management plan, as mentioned in my cut, can the Minister of State provide a projected timeline, even an indicative one, for when all the remaining Town Councils can expect to be covered, maybe especially Sengkang?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Give us that time for us to test whether the half height netting works.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And at the end of the trial period next year, we will share all of the findings to all Town Councils, and we welcome Town Councils to also share their feedback as well as their suggestions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I would also just say that there is no standardisation because different HDB blocks and different aircon ledges have different specifications.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, let us do the trial – 35 – and we will commit to sharing that outcome with all Town Councils.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen
text: Chairman, hon Member Hui Ying has already asked my question.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Dennis Tan, you had another clarification, or not?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Oh, Senior Parliamentary Secretary Dr Syed Harun, can you state your intention?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: Mr Henry Kwek, may I invite you to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Chairman, I thank MND for responding to our cuts and I seek leave to withdraw my amendments.
